pass_a_gloss: Someone will say these things were spoken to Israel, but you are drawing them to those from the nations; we want to show that not after many things, but immediately, wherever he wishes to speak to Israel about repentance, he adds the name of Israel; next it is said: 'If Israel returns, the Lord says, to me, and he will return; and if he removes his abominations from his mouth, and from before my face he will be afraid, and he will swear: As the Lord lives in truth and in judgment and in righteousness, and nations will bless themselves in him'; therefore the first things were said to those from the nations, nations; since when the fullness of the nations enters, then all Israel will be saved, according to what was said by the apostle in the letter to the Romans; consider how God urges us who are returning to return completely, promising that if 'those returning' return to him, he will heal our 'broken fragments' through Jesus Christ; but we, answering, those not intending nor delaying concerning salvation as that Israel, say: 'These we shall be to you'; the God said: 'Return, sons returning, and I will heal your broken fragments'; but those from the nations: 'We shall be slaves,' not formerly 'yours,' but being demons, but encountering opposing powers; for when the Most High divided the nations, we became not a portion of you nor with the people of Jacob a cord of inheritance, but we have become portions of others; yet we, having become portions at some time, when you said to us 'Return, sons returning, and I will heal your broken fragments,' we answer: 'These we are'; for this we await, the call, not as they were called and refused, so we also, being called, refuse; for we have in the parables of the gospel that some called beforehand, one says: 'Take me a wife divorced,' another: 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, I go to test them, take me a wife divorced'; not so we, those from the nations, were called and we refuse; why? Concerning what field that we may be begotten? Concerning what wise woman? But concerning what else shall we be occupied? Therefore God has said to us: 'Return, sons returning, and I will heal your broken fragments'; and seeing our broken fragments and the promise of healing, we immediately answer and say: 'Behold we shall be to you, because you are the Lord our God'; having heard and having said 'We shall be to you,' let us remember that we promised to God, saying to him 'We shall be to you,' and having said to him 'We shall be to you,' let us become nothing else, not a spirit of wrath, not a spirit of grief, not a spirit of desire, not the devil, not his angels; but having been called and having said 'Behold we shall be to you,' we will show to the deserted ones that to become his, to no other but himself we have dedicated ourselves; and we say: 'Because you are the Lord our God you are'; for we do not confess any god (not the belly as the gluttons, 'whose god is the belly,' nor silver as the covetous, and greed, which is idolatry, nor anything else we make out of God and make into God, as many make into God, but to us the God over all, the over all, the through the one in all things God is); and since we have attached ourselves to the toward God, the indeed love attaches us to God) we say: 'These we shall be to you, because you are the Lord our God'.

variants.note: Μνῶν in lock treated as ἐθνῶν ('nations'), not Moab; Pass A corrected.
